changelog: Cut Kaggle training time from ~10.5 to ~2.5-3 GPU-hours without lowering quality. The real v12 run measured ~27.5s per step at seq 1024 plus a ~7.5-minute eval pass every 50 steps, mostly spent re-evaluating identical data - a third of the weekly GPU quota per run. Training now uses seq length 512 (still covering every guidance row), one epoch for 5000+ samples where the loss already converged to 0.39 within a fraction of one epoch, and evaluates only once at the end, keeping the eval-loss gate that blocks blind deploys. The CI deploy also moved out of the trigger workflow: an hourly Deploy LoRA Adapter (Kernel Sweeper) workflow checks the kernel status, skips adapters already deployed via a freshness comparison against the live Cloudflare fine-tune, and uploads the adapter with repository secrets - GitHub jobs no longer wait hours for Kaggle inside the trigger run. Previous release: deployed the trained LoRA adapter from CI instead of Kaggle secrets.
